title: Trofie al Pesto
subtitle: ligurian hand-rolled pasta with basil pesto and potatoes
excerpt: Trofie al Pesto is the definitive dish of Liguria, pairing hand-twisted pasta with a vibrant basil pesto made by pounding basil, pine nuts, garlic and parmesan together in a pestle and mortar. Potatoes and green beans are cooked in the same pan as the pasta, so the whole dish comes together in one pot. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Trofie al Pesto is the emblematic dish of the Ligurian coast, particularly around Genoa. Pesto alla Genovese is protected by a consortium of Ligurian producers and the original recipe specifies Ligurian basil, which has smaller leaves and a sweeter flavour than other varieties.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Ligurian sauce made by crushing basil, pine nuts, garlic, parmesan and olive oil together.
Short twisted Ligurian pasta, traditionally hand-rolled by pressing and rolling small pieces of dough.

content.text: Trofie al Pesto is built around two things: the pasta and the sauce.
are short, tightly twisted little lengths of pasta that hold sauce in their ridges and spirals. Making the
by hand in a pestle and mortar produces a rougher, more textured sauce than a blender would, and the flavour is noticeably fresher. This recipe serves 4.

Potatoes and green beans cook in the same boiling water as the pasta, which is a Ligurian habit that adds body to the dish and saves washing up. Add the potatoes first, then the pasta, then the beans so everything finishes at the same time.

Make the pesto first. Pound the garlic with a pinch of coarse salt in the pestle and mortar until it forms a paste. Add the pine nuts and pound to a rough paste. Add the basil leaves a handful at a time and grind in a circular motion until broken down. Work in the parmesan, then stir in the olive oil. Set aside.
Bring a large pan of water to the boil. Season generously. Add the potato cubes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add 350g of dried trofie to the pan and cook according to packet instructions, usually around 8 to 10 minutes. In the last 3 minutes, add 150g of trimmed green beans to the pan.
Save two ladles of pasta water, then drain everything together in a colander.
Return the pasta, potatoes and beans to the warm pan. Add the pesto and a splash of pasta water. Toss until everything is coated, adding more water to loosen if needed. Season to taste.
Divide between four bowls and finish with a little extra grated parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve straight away.

attrs.symptom: Pesto has turned dark and slightly bitter
attrs.cause: Basil was overworked in a blender, which heats and oxidises it
attrs.fix: Use a pestle and mortar and work quickly with a light hand; the sauce should be rough-textured and bright green

attrs.symptom: Sauce is too thick and clumps around the pasta
attrs.cause: Not enough pasta water added when tossing
attrs.fix: Add the pasta water a spoonful at a time while tossing; it emulsifies the oil and gives the sauce a glossy, flowing consistency

attrs.symptom: Potatoes are falling apart by the time the pasta is cooked
attrs.cause: Potatoes were cut too small or added too early
attrs.fix: Cut potatoes into 1.5cm cubes and start them only 5 minutes before the pasta goes in

content.text: Trofie al Pesto is eaten from Genoa to the Cinque Terre villages every day of the week. It is the kind of food that locals order without looking at the menu. Ligurian basil has its own protected status and the locals argue it is the only basil worth using. Regular supermarket basil works perfectly well for this recipe.
